questions.q: In the IaaS model, such as an AWS EC2 instance or an Azure Virtual Machine, which layer does the customer start managing?
options: The physical datacenter and network backbone
The hypervisor that creates the virtual machine
The operating system, upward through the application and data
Nothing — the provider manages the entire stack
questions.explain: IaaS gives you a virtual machine; the provider manages the hardware and virtualization, and you manage the OS, runtime, application, and data.

questions.q: Azure App Service and AWS Elastic Beanstalk are real examples of which service model?
options: IaaS
PaaS
SaaS
None of these — they are networking products, not cloud service models
questions.explain: Both are Platform as a Service products: you deploy application code and the provider manages the OS and runtime underneath it.

questions.q: What is the key difference between PaaS and SaaS?
options: PaaS has no real-world examples; SaaS does
In PaaS you deploy and manage your own application; in SaaS the application itself is fully managed by the provider
SaaS always costs more than PaaS
PaaS requires a physical datacenter you own; SaaS does not
questions.explain: PaaS still requires you to build and manage an application on top of a managed OS and runtime. SaaS gives you a finished, fully managed application like Microsoft 365 or Salesforce.

questions.q: Across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS, which layer of the stack stays the customer's responsibility in every single model?
options: The physical hardware
The hypervisor
The operating system
The data
questions.explain: Even in fully managed SaaS products, the data you put into the application remains your responsibility — a point the shared responsibility model builds on directly.

questions.q: A team wants to deploy a web application without managing servers, patching an OS, or configuring a runtime themselves. Which service model fits best?
options: IaaS, because it gives the most control
PaaS, because the provider manages the OS and runtime while the team manages only the app and its data
SaaS, because there is no application to build
None of these models would work for this scenario
questions.explain: PaaS products like Azure App Service or AWS Elastic Beanstalk are built exactly for this: deploy code, let the platform handle the OS and runtime.
